where: crates/blaze-cli/src/engine_times.rs write (the 'floor' line); blaze-std Scope::narrow_workers and Scope::may_overlap; engine_bodies.rs/engine_heads.rs time a task as its thread's wall (clock.now().since(began))
what: tempo's profile (score-c1725wave42) printed Bodies wall / floor 0.89: the 'floor' max(largest task, task ms / 16 workers) was above the wall it should bound. Task ms is each task's thread wall (preemption in it), and narrow_workers sets a count without capping how many may_overlap jobs run at once: a job runs on whichever pool worker starts it, or on its joiner. 62.4 s x 16 / 55.3 s says about 18 tasks' clocks ran at once on average.
cost: a floor that read as broken until the pool's semantics were read
cause: a bound that divides thread wall time by a configured worker count assumes task time is CPU time and that no more than that many ran at once; neither held
whys: the floor was written from the rule (largest task, work / workers) without checking what a task's ms measures or what narrow_workers guarantees
class: a lower bound computed from a configured limit instead of a measured one
prevention: engine_times.rs now records each pool job's thread stretch (Times::job) and divides by the most that ran at once, measured, per barrier step; the old division is printed beside it as 'no bound'. A CPU-time bound needs each job's thread CPU time (CLOCK_THREAD_CPUTIME_ID), which bstd does not expose yet
annoyance: narrow_workers reads as a cap on concurrency and is not one
workaround: read 'the most at once' on the floor line
state: fixed in the profile; the pool's cap is not changed
